source_caption:
Still one of the funniest scenes in Tarantino’s universe 🤣

Inglourious Basterds (2009) takes place in an alternate version of World War II, following a group of Jewish-American soldiers hunting Na*is across occupied France, while a young Jewish woman plans her own revenge. With Brad Pitt, Christoph Waltz, Mélanie Laurent, Michael Fassbender, Diane Kruger, and Eli Roth, Tarantino turns a war movie into something completely his own.

What makes the film so good is how much tension comes from conversations rather than action. The opening farmhouse scene and the infamous tavern sequence can feel more intense than most shootouts.

And there are some great stories behind the scenes. Tarantino spent almost a decade working on the script, and at one point he considered abandoning the movie because he couldn’t find anyone who could play Hans Landa. Then Christoph Waltz auditioned — and the rest is history. His performance earned him an Oscar for Best Supporting Actor.

Another fun detail: only around 30% of the movie is spoken in English. Much of it is in French and German, with some Italian — something pretty unusual for a major Hollywood production. 

Even the fictional movie Nation’s Pride was filmed as a real production. Eli Roth directed it, shooting around 180 setups over three days for a film-within-the-film that runs just over five minutes. 

Tarantino didn’t just make a World War II movie. He made a movie about movies, revenge, propaganda, and the power of storytelling — with some of the most memorable characters of his career.

Have you seen Inglourious Basterds? Where does it rank among Tarantino’s films?

source_details.synopsis: Inglourious Basterds is a 2009 war film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino. It stars an ensemble cast including Brad Pitt, Christoph Waltz, Michael Fassbender, Eli Roth, Diane Kruger, Daniel Brühl, Til Schweiger, and Mélanie Laurent. The film tells an alternate history story of two converging plots to assassinate Nazi Germany's leadership at a Paris cinema—one through a British operation largely carried out by a team of Jewish American soldiers led by First Lieutenant Aldo Raine (Pitt), and another by French Jewish cinema proprietor Shosanna Dreyfus (Laurent) who seeks to avenge her murdered family. Both are pitted against Hans Landa (Waltz), an SS colonel with a fearsome reputation.
